modal_verbs.citation: Hyland, K. (2005). Metadiscourse in Academic Writing: Defining the discipline. Journal of English for Academic Purposes, 4(2), 95-113. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.jeap.2004.07.001
modal_verbs.description: Epistemic modal verbs that express possibility, probability, or conditionality in place of direct assertion

epistemic_adverbs.citation: Lakoff, G. (1973). Hedges: A study in meaning criteria and the logic of fuzzy concepts. Journal of Philosophical Logic, 2(4), 458-508. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00262952
epistemic_adverbs.description: Adverbs that modify the degree of certainty or likelihood of a proposition, central to Lakoff's foundational hedging theory

approximators.citation: Kilicoglu, H., & Bergler, S. (2011). Adapting a general semantic web extraction system to biomedical texts. In Proceedings of the International Workshop on BioNLP: Shared Task (p. 92-100). Association for Computational Linguistics.
approximators.description: Approximative terms that hedge by indicating estimates, ranges, or non-precise quantities rather than exact assertions

evidential_frames.citation: Vincze, V., Szarvas, G., Farkas, R., Móra, G., & Csirik, J. (2008). The Szeged Corpus: A tagged database of clinical narratives. In Proceedings of the International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC) (p. 661-666).
evidential_frames.description: Hedging frames that attribute statements to sources, reports, or subjective interpretation rather than asserting them directly

knowledge_shields.citation: Hyland, K. (1998). Hedging in Scientific Research Articles. John Benjamins Publishing Company. https://doi.org/10.1075/pbns.54
knowledge_shields.description: Explicit expressions of limited knowledge, uncertainty, or gaps in understanding that hedge assertions about facts or causality

tentative_language.citation: Salager-Meyer, F. (1994). Hedges and textual communicative function in medical English written discourse. English for Specific Purposes, 13(2), 149-170. https://doi.org/10.1016/0889-4906(94)90013-2
tentative_language.description: Adjectives and constructions that reduce commitment to claims by marking them as tentative, preliminary, or subject to revision

quantifier_hedges.citation: Marín, R. (2010). Gradability and Measurement Construals in Natural Language. Cambridge Scholars Publishing. ISBN: 978-1-4438-2218-2
quantifier_hedges.description: Quantified expressions that hedge by restricting scope or applying domain-limiting modifiers to statements

negation_hedges.citation: Hyland, K. (2005). Metadiscourse in Academic Writing: Defining the discipline. Journal of English for Academic Purposes, 4(2), 95-113. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.jeap.2004.07.001
negation_hedges.description: Negative or restrictive formulations that hedge by framing statements narrowly rather than broadly
